name: Jehoash
bio: Jehoash (Joash), son of Jehoahaz, became king of Israel in Samaria and reigned sixteen years, doing evil in the LORD's eyes like Jeroboam before him (2 Kings 13:10-11). When Elisha lay dying, Jehoash came to him weeping, calling him "my father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof." Elisha had him shoot an arrow eastward as a sign of victory over Syria, then told him to strike the ground with his remaining arrows; Jehoash struck only three times, and Elisha, angry, told him he should have struck five or six times for complete victory — now he would only defeat Syria three times (2 Kings 13:14-19). After Hazael died and his son Ben-Hadad succeeded him, Jehoash recovered the Israelite cities Hazael had taken from his father Jehoahaz, defeating Ben-Hadad three times exactly as Elisha had foretold (2 Kings 13:22-25). His war against Amaziah, king of Judah, is told in detail in the chapters ahead.
